lina: FYI receiving an escalated ticket from Acme — they say when their agent fanout runs two tools in parallel the results sometimes get swapped between tools.
sam: ugh. any logs or repro steps from them?
lina: yes, they sent a minimal repro. They fanout `fetch_customer_profile` and `query_inventory` concurrently. Sometimes the response for profile shows inventory JSON and vice versa.
kevin: can you paste their request body?
lina: here (sanitized):
```json
{
  "input": "lookup order 319",
  "function_calls": [
    { "name": "fetch_customer_profile", "args": {"customer_id": "C319"} },
    { "name": "query_inventory", "args": {"sku": "S-319"} }
  ],
  "mode": "parallel"
}
```
sara: any error codes?
lina: no errors in the API response. The agent returns both tool_results but the `tool_result.metadata.assoc_id` sometimes equals the other tool's call id. So app layer picks the wrong one.
ops-bot: from logs: 1998887776::request start
ops-bot: routing to runtime pool rp-12
ops-bot: dispatched 2 tool calls -> call_a=uuid:aa11, call_b=uuid:bb22
ops-bot: tool runner emitted result (assoc=aa11) for tool=query_inventory at 1998887782
ops-bot: tool runner emitted result (assoc=aa11) for tool=fetch_customer_profile at 1998887782
kevin: both results have assoc=aa11? that smells like shared buffer or correlation header reused.
sam: do they set a per-tool correlation id in headers? or does the runtime generate them?
lina: runtime is supposed to generate per-tool call ids: X-Tool-Call-ID. But in these logs I see the worker reusing the same seq id when two tool tasks got enqueued to the same worker slot.
sara: can we repro internally?
kevin: I wrote a small script to mimic their fanout, sending two function calls in parallel with low inter-arrival time to our hosted endpoint. Repro rate ~1/200 requests locally. Logs show these two failure patterns: the worker sets cookie key `last_tool_call_id` in shared mem that races across goroutines.
sam: nice catch. Any mitigation we can ship fast?
kevin: short-term: ensure the router attaches a per-task UUID and pass it down via the runtime call payload instead of relying on worker-local mutable state. Also add an assert in the mux: `if receivedAssocId != expected || duplicateAssocId { log + drop }`.
lina: action items?
sam: 1) kevin open a PR with fix to route-level correlation (priority P0) 2) prod patch to add a sanity check and metric for duplicate_assoc_id 3) notify Acme with repro steps + ETA.
kevin: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/1823 — title: "fix: per-tool-call UUID and guard against assoc-id reuse". Contains unit tests that simulate concurrent enqueue.
sara: ops, can we add a temporary feature flag to force serializing tool calls for that customer until patched?
lina: sales/CS asked for a 48h workaround window. I can enable a tenant flag to route their requests to serialized execution.
ops-bot: note: added metric `tool_assoc_id_collisions` -> 0.12% in last 24h for rp-12; highest in region-us-west2.
sam: thanks. lina can you draft the reply to Acme: include repro, root cause (race on worker-local state), mitigation (hotfix + tenant-level serialize) and timeline? keep it simple.
lina: will do, sending draft in a bit. :thumbsup:
kevin: followups: add e2e test for parallel fanout, add leak detection for per-worker mutable state, and plan a rollout to Dedicated/Private (ensure same patch applies).
sara: also check if any telemetry or billing mapping uses assoc ids — we should validate invoice data mapping.
lina: noted. I'll include for billing ops to sanity-check mappings for affected time windows.
sam: thanks team. If anyone sees a customer hit with 5+ occurrences escalate me directly.
kevin: pushing a small-hotfix to canary now.
ops-bot: deploy canary -> rp-12a at 1998887815 -> success
lina: thanks, everyone. I'll update ticket and ping when ACME confirms the fix.
sam: great work.
